original_test_intent.purpose: Verify the SMBIOS Type 7 System Cache Type enumeration for every required cache record and confirm each mapped value remains correct after reboot.
original_test_intent.target: Type 7 offset 11h System Cache Type for all owner-required cache structures, mapped by handle/designation/configuration level and Type 4 processor-cache references.
original_test_intent.scope: Read and compare the standard DMTF enum—Other, Unknown, Instruction, Data or Unified—before and after one approved reboot. The item text's leading `Cache` is a redundant catalog prefix, not evidence of a second vendor-specific field.
original_test_intent.operation: Collect complete Type 4/Type 7 data, map every required cache record, extract the standard System Cache Type byte/decoded enum, compare with the owner topology, obtain reboot approval, repeat the same collection/mapping and verify persistence plus host/management health.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: Two read-only captures separated by one approved reboot; no cache-setting write or performance workload is specified.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every required cache is present and mapped; its standard System Cache Type enum matches the approved instruction/data/unified topology (or an explicitly accepted Other/Unknown case) before and after reboot; no record or platform-health regression occurs.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/CPU/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode identity, owner per-handle/socket/level expected enum, complete pre/post Type 4 and Type 7 structures, raw byte/decoded enum, stable handle mapping, comparison, reboot timeline and OS/BMC health.
ambiguities: The source omits expected enum values and multi-socket cache mapping.
The DeepSeek literal grep cannot match the canonical dmidecode label.
The source procedure does not explicitly state the reboot that its criterion requires.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly detects that the literal grep label is wrong, but over-blocks the testcase by treating a redundant catalog prefix as an unresolved target. DMTF defines exactly one Type 7 field at offset 11h named System Cache Type, and adjacent rows systematically prefix canonical Type 7 fields with `Cache`, providing sufficient evidence to preserve the intended standard field without inventing a new test.

applicable_history.decision: The neighboring Type 7 item names use the repeated pattern `Type 7 - Cache Information - Cache <canonical field>` for Cache Speed, Cache Error Correction Type, Cache System Cache Type and Cache Associativity; this is a catalog naming convention, not distinct vendor-field evidence.
The historical review follows the literal nonmatching grep and provides no authoritative field mapping.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify BLOCKED to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. The target is the standard Type 7 System Cache Type field; remaining expected-enum, mapping, package and reboot inputs are provisionable readiness conditions, while pre-reboot actual values can be collected safely now.

revision_candidate.test_name: SMBIOS Type 7 System Cache Type Persistence
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify the standard SMBIOS Type 7 System Cache Type enum for every required cache record and confirm the mapped values remain correct after one reboot.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact CPU/server recipe and BIOS/SMBIOS build with an approved cache topology, validated dmidecode access, an approved reboot window and working console/BMC/OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All required Type 7 offset-11h System Cache Type fields, mapped by structure handle, designation, cache level and Type 4 L1/L2/L3 references. Do not search for a nonexistent `Cache System Cache Type` output label.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Expected enum per cache instance; CPU/socket/cache and Type 4/Type 7 mapping; policy for Other/Unknown; dmidecode version/package and sudo access; host credentials; reboot approval, workload isolation, power/OOB recovery and evidence destination.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Collect complete pre-reboot Type 4 and Type 7 structures; map all required caches; extract and compare each standard System Cache Type raw/decoded value; after explicit approval reboot once; repeat the identical collection/mapping/comparison and verify OS/BMC health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct SUT/CPU/BIOS selected; expected cache enum map signed; dmidecode validated; least-privilege access available; workload quiesced; reboot window, power and OOB recovery ready; existing logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Signed per-cache expected map; platform and tool versions; unfiltered pre/post Type 4/Type 7 output; handle/link table; raw and decoded System Cache Type enums; exact comparison; reboot timeline; OS/BMC health and exceptions.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: DMTF DSP0134 SMBIOS 3.9.0 Type 7 offset 11h and Table 39 enum semantics, plus the exact platform CPU/cache topology specification supplying each expected value.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Use read-only SMBIOS collection only. Do not change cache/CPU/firmware state, run the known-wrong grep, omit instances, invent topology, clear logs or reboot without approval and recovery.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Platform owner supplies and accepts the enum map; system/workload owner approves reboot and resolves discrepancies. Ordinary pre-reboot read-only collection needs no additional approval.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners provide acceptance data and reboot authorization. Once supplied, collection, structure linking, enum decoding, comparison and approved reboot orchestration can be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If reboot or management recovery fails, stop and use approved console/BMC/OOB recovery. On missing, duplicate, Other/Unknown or changed records, preserve complete dumps and firmware context; do not alter cache settings under this case.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing expected enum/map, unresolved Type 4/Type 7 link, incomplete output, unapproved Other/Unknown, pre-test mismatch, absent reboot approval/recovery, boot/management failure or post-reboot handle/enum drift.
